items.title: Live: Albanese promises to do 'everything' to protect Australians from worst of war
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese delivers an address to the nation on the government response to war in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: PM says next months 'may not be easy', urges Australians to save fuel
items.description: Anthony Albanese asks Australians to trade their cars for public transport if they can, while reassuring those who need to drive they can continue to do so amid the global oil crisis.

items.title: PM's warning shot could backfire to create the panic he wants to avoid
items.description: The prime minister risks criticism for using the rare measure of a national address to urge calm without announcing any new measures.

items.title: Keep track of today's sharp drop in petrol prices around the country
items.description: The federal government's cut to fuel excise has almost immediately flowed through to petrol prices at the pump, according to ABC tracking of fuel price data nationwide.

items.title: 'Ridiculous': How Australians are coping with sky-high fuel prices
items.description: The ABC asked how you were coping with fuel prices and here's what we heard back.

items.title: Why it's a 'no-brainer' that teachers are fleeing this broken system
items.description: Victoria bills itself as the 'education state' but a growing exodus of teachers and underfunding has that tag under threat.

items.title: Anthropic boss makes big call on Australian copyright dispute
items.description: The AI company's billionaire boss says he is not trying to convince Australia to change its mind on protecting the copyright of artists.

items.title: Study shows gen Z craves in-person connection more than other generations
items.description: Gen Z is embracing retro technology like iPods, vinyl and Polaroid cameras and craves in-person connection more than any other generation, according to a Live Nation study.

items.title: Arnold carried in jubilant scenes after Iraq qualifies for World Cup
items.description: Former Socceroos coach Graham Arnold has guided Iraq to their first FIFA World Cup appearance in 40 years with a playoff win over Bolivia.

items.title: Inside Queensland's first recovery village for eating disorder survivors
items.description: A couple whose daughters survived eating disorders is opening a first-of-its-kind recovery village to help survivors ease back into their normal lives without relapsing.

items.title: Former Sydney University lecturer seen in Iran video about Hormuz Strait
items.description: An Australian academic has appeared in an Iranian propaganda video supporting a toll system imposed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on foreign merchant shipping.

items.title: Dezi Freeman investigation to probe January bushfires 1km from hiding spot
items.description: Victoria Police have officially confirmed that the person shot dead by officers at a property in Victoria's north-east on Monday morning was fugitive Dezi Freeman.

items.title: Dire future of superb fairy-wren could mean catastrophe for other species
items.description: The researchers said the superb fairy-wren would likely go extinct within 30-40 years unless action was taken to stop greenhouse gas emissions causing climate change.

items.title: How this Aussie went from TAFE to the head of Sony character animation
items.description: Daniel Pozo has had a hand in Sony hits like Spiderman: Across the Spider-Verse and Hotel Transylvania, but GOAT is his first project in the driver's seat.

items.title: Lawsuit filed against Taylor Swift over The Life of a Showgirl album
items.description: Las Vegas performer Maren Wade says the name and imagery of Taylor Swift's latest album are too close to those of her show, Confessions of a Showgirl.

items.title: Bluey's lead composer on helping kids fall in love with music
items.description: A new orchestral Bluey album is out. Lead composer Joff Bush talks about classical music, storytelling and inspiring kids to love music.

items.title: National addresses are rare and historic. Now, Albanese has made another
items.description: Pandemics, wars, and landmark moments have been immortalised in addresses to the nation. Anthony Albanese has become one of the few prime ministers to employ the form.

items.title: Crucial exhibits unveiled to jury in Irma Palasics cold case trial
items.description: A milk container and water jug carrying DNA evidence were revealed to jurors as a decades-old murder trial reached its final stage.

items.title: Australia's solar panel waste issue is growing in size year-on-year
items.description: Australians are expected to throw away 90,000 tonnes of solar panel waste each year by 2030, a federal government hearing has been told.

items.title: New mine owner claims he's faced threats over removing bikie shareholders
items.description: The Tasmanian government has taken steps to revoke the operating licence of one of the state's biggest mining operations, after being warned it was allegedly used as a "vehicle for money laundering" and former owners were associated with underworld figures.

items.title: Share markets energised as they price in end to Iran war, but there's a catch
items.description: If you had woken up today and heard someone say Wall Street's tech sector rose more than 3 per cent overnight, you would expect it to be promptly followed by "April Fools' Day".

items.title: NBL owner prepared to walk away from major land purchase
items.description: After the Tasmanian government was urged to abandon the sale of prime waterfront land but chose to persevere, it now appears the developer is prepared to "walk away" from the potential purchase.

items.title: Cultural compensation replaces fine in 'rare' illegal logging ruling
items.description: Traditional owners say a $450,000 fine will not replace the six centuries-old giant trees illegally felled by NSW Forestry Corporation.

items.title: Fears for stingray populations as algal bloom moves north
items.description: Evidence of South Australia's harmful algal bloom has been detected in previously untouched parts of the Spencer Gulf days after rays were seen gathering in shallow waters.

items.title: 'We are an expert': How Lebanon's airport keeps running despite Israeli strikes
items.description: Beirut-Rafic Hariri Airport, Lebanon's gateway to the world, is still operating even as Israel bombards its surroundings.
